clue.text: Conflict I head, exhibiting caution

parts.note: war is armed conflict
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone at the heart of a conflict proceeds with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' here is geographical: NESS, as in Loch Ness's neighbours, is a headland or promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a careful, wary attitude towards possible danger, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: River taking sailor into North Sea inlet

indicators.note: the inlet takes the sailor inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
the inlet takes the sailor inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Wash is a large bay on England's east coast opening into the North Sea
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A river carries a seaman out into a North Sea bay.
explanation.walkthrough: THE WASH is a bay between Lincolnshire and Norfolk in eastern England. The Wabash is a river in the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wabash is a river of Indiana and Ohio, a tributary of the Ohio, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Mature state swan exhibits

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A swan of some standing shows its maturity.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature and to ripen both mean to develop fully, as fruit or ideas do, so they are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Just setting out finally on climb

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word on

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A mountaineer has only just begun the climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is coming into being and beginning to develop, just starting out on its life.

clue.text: Methinks I'd cut out being unadventurous

indicators.note: out signals that the preceding words are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters ID

explanation.surface: A bold talker declares that being timid will be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' seems to pair with 'cut' as a phrase meaning removed, but it signals the rearrangement. The held clue ends with a stray 'ous', an OCR repeat of the end of 'unadventurous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick-in-the-mud is a person who resists change and novelty, so the phrase works as an adjective for an unadventurous sort.

clue.text: Shoe's tongue

definitions.meaning: a stout leather walking shoe with decorative perforations
a tongue can mean a way of speaking, here a strong regional, especially Irish, accent

explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is both a perforated leather shoe and a marked Irish or Scottish accent of speech.

clue.text: Item written up in right voucher

indicators.note: in places the turned item inside the outer letters

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the word is entered bottom to top, so it is turned round

parts.note: a piece is an item, as in a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: An item noted down sits in the correct receipt.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written acknowledgment of payment, a kind of voucher proving a transaction.

clue.text: Choice of names relating to calendar Andr

parts.note: Greg is a man's name
or is the word offering a choice
Ian is another man's name

explanation.surface: Someone choosing names for a child is told to consult the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choice of names' reads as a selection from a list, but it is literally two names with the word of choice between them. The held clue ends with stray OCR debris from a neighbouring line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gregorian calendar, introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582, is the one in general use today.

clue.text: Writer says "I set out…

indicators.note: out signals the preceding words are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author announces that a journey is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 10 down with its ellipsis, so the quotation seems to continue; 'out' is the anagram signal for SAYS I SET.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is someone who writes essays, a particular kind of writer.

clue.text: Getting round like this you fail to bid

definitions.text: like this you fail to bid
definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., the way a card player declines to bid at bridge

explanation.definitionFit: Bypassing means going round an obstacle, and by passing describes declining a bid at the card table.

clue.text: "… to join in profitable activity, once that gent and I reach an arrangement"

indicators.note: the words agreeing on an arrangement signal that their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone speaks of teaming up with a gentleman once they have struck a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the fodder and gives no letters: the anagram is of ONCE, THAT GENT and I. The ellipsis carries on from 8 down's quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To get in on the act is an idiom for joining in an activity, especially a successful or lucrative one.

clue.text: This is played on board ship by revolutionary

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A game is played aboard a vessel alongside a famous revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' looks like it means aboard the ship, but it is part of the definition: a game played on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a game played on a chequered board of sixty-four squares.

clue.text: Part of vessel that's foundered, about last month

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a vessel that has foundered has sunk
December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year

explanation.surface: A ship went down at the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundeck is an upper deck of a ship where passengers can sit in the sun, so it is part of a vessel.

clue.text: Hear about one record in a series

indicators.note: about puts the first piece around the following pair

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
I is the Roman numeral one
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Listening to one recording that belongs to a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is legal: a court hears, or tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilogy is a series of three related works, such as novels or films.

clue.text: Means of punishing malicious woman, one hiding in shadows

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful or malicious woman

indicators.note: one hides the following word inside itself

parts.note: taken as written
to shadow someone is to tail them, so shadows is tails

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman lurks in the shadows, ready to punish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hiding in' tempts the solver to use I for one; here the whole word stays and swallows the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip of knotted cords used for flogging, especially in the navy.

clue.text: Be persuaded to visit

definitions.meaning: to change one's opinion and agree, as in she'll eventually agree

explanation.definitionFit: Come round means both to be won over to another view and to pay someone a visit.

clue.text: Do old fit into slipper maiden's lost?

indicators.note: fit into means placed inside the other piece
lost means that letter is dropped from the shoe

parts.note: a moccasin is a soft slipper-like shoe
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A question about whether an old man can squeeze into a slipper that has lost its girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the noun: a party or function. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a social event or party, and an occasion is a special event or celebration.

clue.text: Grasp loosely — no more pinches

indicators.note: loosely suggests the words are put together in a loose, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Hold something gently, without squeezing any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasp as a noun means understanding, as in a good grasp of the facts, which is what comprehension is.

clue.text: Rave about old film, being most objectionable

indicators.note: about means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: to rant is to rave
Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: Ranting about a dated movie that someone finds deeply offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: KES is a classic 1969 British film set in a Yorkshire mining town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means offensive or foul, so rankest is the superlative, most objectionable.

clue.text: Vet gets list of requirements in in time

indicators.note: the first in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a spec, a specification, lists what is required

explanation.surface: A vet receives the specifications just before the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to check or examine it carefully, which is to inspect it.

clue.text: Foolhardy military assistant involved in plan

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
ADC is aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a senior commander

explanation.surface: A reckless aide gets caught up in the battle plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes behaviour that is wildly impulsive and reckless.

clue.text: Friend caught by a motorway radar, for one

indicators.note: caught by means the friend is held inside the other letters

parts.note: M is short for motorway, as in the M1
a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: A pal is nabbed by a speed camera on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radar' looks like a speed trap in the surface, but it is the definition: RADAR is formed from Radio Detection And Ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is built from the initials of radio detection and ranging, so it is an example of such a word.

clue.text: Biblical book with girl giving shout of praise

parts.note: HOS is the abbreviation for the book of Hosea
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl reading scripture lets out a joyful cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is an exclamation of adoration and praise to God, used in Christian worship.

clue.text: Pole playing a part in minor theatricals

indicators.note: playing a part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Polish actor takes a small role in amateur dramatics.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Pole is one of the Earth's two poles, so north names a pole.

clue.text: Hurt, Jack quits, displaying temper

indicators.note: quits means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: to injure is to hurt
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: Injured, a man called Jack walks out in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' is the verb meaning to toughen, not an angry mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to harden or accustom someone to hardship, just as steel is tempered.

clue.text: Am I direct, if misguided? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: misguided suggests the letters are led astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are too blunt, and is told they are the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Diametric means directly opposed, as two points at opposite ends of a diameter are.

clue.text: Altogether original song auditioned

indicators.note: auditioned means the phrase is heard rather than read, so it is said aloud

parts.note: a new ditty is an original song

explanation.surface: An original song is tried out at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the altogether' is an idiom for being naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the altogether is to be naked, so the word stands for nakedness by idiom.

clue.text: Mend frame

definitions.meaning: to set someone up falsely for a crime

explanation.definitionFit: Stitch up means to repair with sewing, and a stitch-up is a frame-up of an innocent person.
